name: Watari-um
funding: Founded by Shizuko Watari in 1990 out of her Galerie Watari; the owner's residence is in the building.
watch: Self-funded family museum with no published budget. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The private museum's site lists membership tiers but no annual reports, accounts, donor names or board.

name: Wave Hill
funding: FY2025 expenses $9.4M; 26% government (city-owned site), 31% contributions and grants, 25% investment income.
watch: The FY25 report names only the board and Leadership Council, none flagged; corporate, foundation and government funders are not named.
records_note: Posts the FY2025 annual report with a financial summary, its 2025 Form 990 and a named board; no donor list is published.

name: White Columns
funding: Expenses $1.3M (FY2025). NYC DCLA and NYSCA; Warhol, Frankenthaler, Speyer, Niarchos, Luce and Blavatnik Family foundations, as listed on its 2025 support page.
watch: Blavatnik Family Foundation (Access Industries, oil origin) is contested at Tate and Oxford.
records_note: Names donors and foundations with a 2025 benefit sponsor heading and lists its board; no annual report, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: WHW (What, How & for Whom) / Galerija Nova
funding: City of Zagreb City Office for Culture, Ministry of Culture of Croatia, Foundation for Arts Initiatives; non-profit collective.

name: Winnipeg Art Gallery-Qaumajuq
funding: 2024 donor list: Canada, Manitoba, City of Winnipeg, Nunavut; TD Bank Group ($100-249k), Canada Life, Power Corporation, RBC, Manitoba Liquor & Lotteries, Richardson, Asper Foundation.
records_note: Its site blocks automated access; search results show annual reports from 2014-15 to 2024-25 with a supporter list, summary statements and a named board chair.

name: Wits Art Museum
funding: University of the Witwatersrand museum. Standard Bank has been collection partner since 1978 and 1979; early donors include Norman Herber, Jack Ginsberg, John Schlesinger and Gertrude Posel.
watch: The May 2024 Wits encampment concerned university policy, not this museum.
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; its parent Wits University posts annual reports 2006 to 2025 with financial statements and lists its Council.

name: Wysing Arts Centre
funding: £863k income (FY2025); ACE NPO, Freelands Fdn (Murdoch media money), Garfield Weston, Ragdoll, Art Fund, local councils, Thalia Waste.
watch: Funders include Thalia Waste Management (landfill fund) and the John Armitage Charitable Trust (hedge-fund money), both allowed.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; the support page names funders, undated; a board of trustees is listed.

name: Ў Gallery of Contemporary Art
records_note: Closed on 29 October 2020; its domain now shows only a default web-server page, with no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media (YCAM)
funding: FY2021 programme budget ¥305M: 88.7% Yamaguchi City, 3.3% Agency for Cultural Affairs grants. The 2026 show is funded by the same two.
watch: Municipal media-art centre. The latest published budget breakdown is FY2021. Corporate links are commissioned R&D only (Sony CSL, Mitsukoshi Isetan).
records_note: YCAM posts annual reports for FY2009 to FY2021 with a programme outturn table, but no funder list and no named board.

name: Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Municipal autonomous institution; founder Department of Culture of the Yekaterinburg city administration; Hermitage-Ural centre opened 2021.
records_note: It posts yearly reports 2014 to 2023, financial results 2014 to 2024 and the supervisory board's composition orders, but no sponsor list.

name: Yemisi Shyllon Museum of Art
funding: University museum opened 2019, endowed by collector Prince Yemisi Shyllon; free entry from June 2026 paid by Aisha and Gbenga Oyebode.
watch: On the Pan-Atlantic University campus. Its 2026 free-admission funder chairs a palm-oil firm in a land dispute.
records_note: Annual reports 2020 to 2025 give income shares but no accounts; sponsor logos are undated; the supervisory council and advisory board are named.

name: Yokohama Museum of Art
funding: FY2024 income ¥1.10B: ¥881M city management fee through the Yokohama Arts Foundation, ¥91M own projects, ¥23M fees, ¥40M city support. Five HEART to ART corporate partners.
records_note: The museum posts reports and settled accounts for FY2020 to FY2024 and names corporate supporters, undated; its operator posts a dated board list.
